prophets|title: The age of the prophets, the messengers and the revealed scriptures
prophets|subtitle: From Adam (peace be upon him) to Isa (peace be upon him)
prophets|summary: Twenty-three prophets and messengers in a single chain of tawhid (the oneness of God), and with them the revealed scriptures: the Scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa, the Torah, the Psalms (Zabur), and the Gospel (Injil).
prophets|when.hijri: Until just before the Prophet's birth
prophets/first-fathers/adam|subtitle: Father of humankind and first of the prophets
prophets/first-fathers/adam|lines.0: Standing and description: Allah created him with His own Hand, breathed into him of His spirit, made His angels prostrate to him, and taught him all the names.
prophets/first-fathers/adam|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: vicegerency on earth, Iblis's refusal and arrogance, the test of the tree of Paradise and the whispering, then repentance and being chosen ﴿فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
prophets/first-fathers/adam|lines.2: Teachings and scriptures: the beginning of tawhid and the first commandments, and repentance and seeking forgiveness.
prophets/first-fathers/sheth|subtitle: Son of Adam (peace be upon him)
prophets/first-fathers/sheth|lines.0: Standing and description: the son of Adam, his successor on earth and his appointed heir in caring for his children and preserving the law of tawhid.
prophets/first-fathers/sheth|lines.1: Context: the generations of believers continued in pure tawhid for ten centuries between Adam and Nuh.
prophets/first-fathers/idris|lines.0: Standing and description: a noble prophet whom Allah praised for truthfulness and patience; the Prophet ﷺ met him in the fourth heaven on the night of the Mi'raj (Ascension).
prophets/first-fathers/idris|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: truthfulness, prophethood and an exalted station ﴿وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِدْرِيسَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَّبِيًّا * وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا﴾.
prophets/first-fathers/idris|lines.2: Patience: ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِّنَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾.
prophets/first-messengers|title: Nuh, the first of the messengers, and the first nations
prophets/first-messengers/nuh|subtitle: The first of the messengers and the elder of the envoys
prophets/first-messengers/nuh|lines.0: Standing and description: the first messenger sent after idolatry (shirk) appeared on earth; one of the messengers of firm resolve (Ulu al-'Azm).
prophets/first-messengers/nuh|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: calling his people for a thousand years less fifty with patience and striving, building the Ark by Allah's revelation, the great Flood, the drowning of his disobedient son, and the rescue of the believers ﴿وَقِيلَ يَا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي مَاءَكِ﴾.
prophets/first-messengers/nuh|lines.2: Teachings: pure tawhid, disowning the idols (Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr), and gratitude for Allah's blessings.
prophets/first-messengers/hud|lines.0: The people and the place: he was sent to the tribe of 'Ad in al-Ahqaf (Hadramawt and the south of the Peninsula), people of towering buildings and might.
prophets/first-messengers/hud|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: reminding them of Allah's blessings and forbidding them tyranny ﴿أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ آيَةً تَعْبَثُونَ * وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ﴾.
prophets/first-messengers/hud|lines.2: The outcome: the people denied him and grew arrogant, so they were destroyed by a furious, roaring wind imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and Allah saved Hud and those who believed with him.
prophets/first-messengers/salih|lines.0: The people and the place: he was sent to Thamud in al-Hijr (the north of the Arabian Peninsula), who skilfully carved homes out of the mountains.
prophets/first-messengers/salih|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: the people asked for a miraculous sign, so Allah brought forth the she-camel for them as a clear sign, and he warned them not to harm her ﴿هَٰذِهِ نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً فَذَرُوهَا تَأْكُلْ فِي أَرْضِ اللَّهِ﴾.
prophets/first-messengers/salih|lines.2: The outcome: the most wretched of them hamstrung the she-camel after their chiefs conspired, so the Blast and the earthquake seized them and they lay lifeless in their homes.
prophets/ibrahim-house|title: The era of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his descendants
prophets/ibrahim-house|subtitle: Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb, Isma'il and Ishaq, Ya'qub, Yusuf
prophets/ibrahim-house/ibrahim|subtitle: The Friend of Allah (Khalil Allah) and leader of the upright in faith (hunafa')
prophets/ibrahim-house/ibrahim|lines.0: Description and place: the leader of tawhid, breaker of idols, one of the messengers of firm resolve, father of the prophets.
prophets/ibrahim-house/ibrahim|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: his argument with the one who disputed with him about his Lord, and his argument with his people; being thrown into the fire, which became coolness and safety; the migration to the blessed land and to Makkah; building the Ka'bah with Isma'il ﴿وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ﴾; and the trial of the great sacrifice.
prophets/ibrahim-house/ibrahim|lines.2: The revealed scripture: the Scrolls of Ibrahim ﴿صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ﴾.
prophets/ibrahim-house/lut|lines.0: Kinship and place: the son of Ibrahim's brother (peace be upon him); he believed with him and migrated with him, then was sent to the people of Sodom in the Jordan Valley.
prophets/ibrahim-house/lut|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: forbidding them the hideous indecency unprecedented in humankind, and facing their aggression ﴿أَتَأْتُونَ الْفَاحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّنَ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
prophets/ibrahim-house/lut|lines.2: The outcome: the angels' visit to Ibrahim and then to Lut, Lut and his family leaving by night, and the destruction of his wife, who stayed behind, together with the people, by a rain of stones and the overturning of their towns upside down.
prophets/ibrahim-house/shuayb|lines.0: The people and the place: he was sent to the people of Madyan and the Companions of the Thicket (al-Aykah) (the north-west of the Arabian Peninsula).
prophets/ibrahim-house/shuayb|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: forbidding them to give short measure and weight, to spread corruption in the land and to waylay travellers ﴿أَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُخْسِرِينَ * وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ﴾.
prophets/ibrahim-house/shuayb|lines.2: The outcome: the chiefs of his people mocked and denied him, so the punishment of the Day of the Shadowing Cloud and the quake of the Blast seized them, and they lay lifeless in their homes as though they had never lived there.
prophets/ibrahim-house/ismail-ishaq|titl: Isma'il and Ishaq (Ishmael and Isaac) (peace be upon them)
prophets/ibrahim-house/ismail-ishaq|line: Isma'il (peace be upon him): true to his promise, the prophet of Makkah, ancestor of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and of the Arabised Arabs; he shared with his father in building the Ka'bah ﴿وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَّبِيًّا﴾.

Ishaq (peace be upon him): the blessed glad tidings to Sarah and Ibrahim in their old age, a noble prophet and the father of Ya'qub; from his line the prophets of the Children of Israel followed one after another ﴿وَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِإِسْحَاقَ نَبِيًّا مِّنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾.
prophets/ibrahim-house/yaqub|lines.0: Lineage and place: the son of Ishaq son of Ibrahim (peace be upon them); he was given the title "Isra'il", and to him all the Children of Israel and their twelve tribes are traced.
prophets/ibrahim-house/yaqub|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: beautiful patience at being parted from his two sons Yusuf and Binyamin ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ﴾, and certainty in Allah's mercy ﴿إِنَّمَا أَشْكُو بَثِّي وَحُزْنِي إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾.
prophets/ibrahim-house/yaqub|lines.2: The final counsel: his everlasting counsel to his sons at his death to hold firm to tawhid and the upright religion ﴿مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن بَعْدِي قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلَٰهَكَ وَإِلَٰهَ آبَائِكَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِلَٰهًا وَاحِدًا﴾.
prophets/ibrahim-house/yusuf|lines.0: Lineage and description: the noble son of the noble son of the noble son of the noble (Yusuf son of Ya'qub son of Ishaq son of Ibrahim); he was given half of all beauty and the knowledge of interpreting dreams.
prophets/ibrahim-house/yusuf|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: the best of stories; his brothers throwing him into the well out of envy, his sale in Egypt, the attempted seduction by the wife of al-'Aziz, patience and chastity in prison, interpreting the king's dream, being established over the storehouses of the land, then the reunion of the family and the prostration of his parents and brothers in fulfilment of the dream ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَاءُ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms|title: From Ayyub to al-Yasa': the Torah and the Psalms
prophets/torah-psalms|subtitle: Ayyub, Dhu al-Kifl, Yunus, Musa and Harun, Yusha', Dawud, Sulayman, Ilyas, al-Yasa'
prophets/torah-psalms/ayyub|subtitle: The symbol of patience and certainty
prophets/torah-psalms/ayyub|lines.0: Standing and description: a noble prophet to whom Allah gave wealth, family and children, then Allah tested him in his body, his wealth and his children, and he was patient.
prophets/torah-psalms/ayyub|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: immense patience without complaining to anyone but Allah, until he became the proverbial example of patience ﴿إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِرًا نِّعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/ayyub|lines.2: The relief: his humble supplication ﴿أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾, so Allah commanded him to strike the ground with his foot ﴿ارْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ هَٰذَا مُغْتَسَلٌ بَارِدٌ وَشَرَابٌ﴾, and Allah restored to him his health and his family, and the like of them along with them, as a mercy and a reminder for the worshippers.
prophets/torah-psalms/dhulkifl|lines.0: Description and mention: Allah the Exalted mentioned him in the Holy Qur'an among the prophets, and praised him for patience and righteousness.
prophets/torah-psalms/dhulkifl|lines.1: In the Qur'an: ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِّنَ الصَّابِرِينَ * وَأَدْخَلْنَاهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِنَا إِنَّهُم مِّنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾, and ﴿وَاذْكُرْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ الْأَخْيَارِ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/yunus|subtitle: Dhu al-Nun, the Companion of the Whale
prophets/torah-psalms/yunus|lines.0: The place and the message: he was sent to the people of Nineveh in Iraq; when he despaired of them he left in anger before his Lord had permitted him.
prophets/torah-psalms/yunus|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: boarding the laden ship, the casting of lots that fell on him, being thrown into the sea and swallowed by the whale.
prophets/torah-psalms/yunus|lines.2: The supplication in distress: his glorification of Allah and his supplication in the darkness of the sea, the night and the belly of the whale ﴿لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/yunus|lines.3: Deliverance and outcome: he was cast onto the open shore and a gourd plant was made to grow over him, and his people repented, which lifted from them the punishment of disgrace ﴿إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/musa-harun|title: Musa and Harun (Moses and Aaron) (peace be upon them)
prophets/torah-psalms/musa-harun|subtitl: The one to whom Allah spoke (Kalim Allah), and the Torah
prophets/torah-psalms/musa-harun|lines.0: Place and description: Musa, the one to whom Allah spoke, one of the messengers of firm resolve; and his brother Harun, his minister, eloquent of tongue.
prophets/torah-psalms/musa-harun|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: the most frequently mentioned story in the Qur'an; his birth and being cast into the river, his upbringing in Pharaoh's palace, his departure to Madyan, Allah speaking to him at Mount Tur, the nine signs and the confrontation with Pharaoh and his magicians, the parting of the sea and the drowning of Pharaoh and his soldiers, and the wandering of the Children of Israel for forty years.
prophets/torah-psalms/musa-harun|lines.2: The revealed scripture: the Torah (on the Tablets) ﴿وَكَتَبْنَا لَهُ فِي الْأَلْوَاحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْعِظَةً وَتَفْصِيلًا لِّكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾, and the Criterion (al-Furqan) as guidance and light.
prophets/torah-psalms/yusha|title: Yusha' ibn Nun (Joshua) (peace be upon him)
prophets/torah-psalms/yusha|lines.0: Description and lineage: the young attendant and disciple of Musa who accompanied him on the journey to the meeting of the two seas to meet al-Khidr ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَاهُ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/yusha|lines.1: The story and standing: the prophet of Allah who took over the leadership of the Children of Israel after the deaths of Musa and Harun in the wilderness, and led them to conquer Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and enter the Holy Land.
prophets/torah-psalms/yusha|lines.2: The prophetic miracle: the sun was held back for him by Allah's command until he completed the conquest, as the Prophet ﷺ reported.
prophets/torah-psalms/dawud|lines.0: Standing and description: a king and a prophet, given a beautiful voice in praising Allah; Allah made iron soft for him, and he made full coats of mail.
prophets/torah-psalms/dawud|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: killing the tyrant Jalut (Goliath) and the victory of Talut (Saul) ﴿وَقَتَلَ دَاوُودُ جَالُوتَ وَآتَاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾, the mountains and the birds glorifying Allah with him morning and evening ﴿يَا جِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ وَالطَّيْرَ﴾, and decisive judgement in disputes.
prophets/torah-psalms/dawud|lines.2: The revealed scripture: the Psalms (Zabur) ﴿وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ زَبُورًا﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/sulayman|subtitle: Son of Dawud and the great king
prophets/torah-psalms/sulayman|lines.0: Standing and description: he inherited prophethood and kingship from Dawud; Allah gave him a kingdom such as befits no one after him.
prophets/torah-psalms/sulayman|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: the subjection of the wind, the jinn and humans to him, understanding the language of animals and birds (the story of the hoopoe and the ant), the story of the throne of Bilqis, Queen of Sheba, and her submission with him to Allah, Lord of the worlds ﴿قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي وَأَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَانَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/sulayman|lines.2: The way: gratitude for blessings and humility before the True King ﴿هَٰذَا مِن فَضْلِ رَبِّي لِيَبْلُوَنِي أَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/ilyas|lines.0: Lineage and place: one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, sent to the people of Baalbek in the Levant.
prophets/torah-psalms/ilyas|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: forbidding his people to worship the idol (Ba'l) and calling them to the Lord of the worlds ﴿أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلًا وَتَذَرُونَ أَحْسَنَ الْخَالِقِينَ * اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ وَرَبَّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/ilyas|lines.2: The Qur'an's praise: his people denied him and so deserved punishment, and Allah made his remembrance everlasting ﴿سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ إِلْ يَاسِينَ * إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
prophets/torah-psalms/alyasa|lines.0: Standing and lineage: the companion of Ilyas (peace be upon him) and his successor in calling the Children of Israel to guidance and the Law.
prophets/torah-psalms/alyasa|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: fragrant praise of him among the best of the prophets ﴿وَاذْكُرْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِّنَ الْأَخْيَارِ﴾, and his being favoured above the worlds in virtue and faith ﴿وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطًا وَكُلًّا فَضَّلْنَا عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
prophets/gospel|title: Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa: the Gospel
prophets/gospel|subtitle: Zakariyya and Yahya, Isa son of Maryam
prophets/gospel/zakariya-yahya|title: Zakariyya and Yahya (Zechariah and John) (peace be upon them)
prophets/gospel/zakariya-yahya|lines.0: Zakariyya (peace be upon him): guardian of Maryam in the prayer niche (mihrab); his secret supplication in old age ﴿رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِي فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ﴾, after which he was given the glad tidings of Yahya.
prophets/gospel/zakariya-yahya|lines.1: Yahya (peace be upon him): the prophet, noble, chaste, dutiful to his parents; he was given wisdom as a child, and held fast to the Torah with strength ﴿يَا يَحْيَىٰ خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍ﴾.
prophets/gospel/isa|title: Isa son of Maryam (Jesus son of Mary) (peace be upon him)
prophets/gospel/isa|subtitle: The Word of Allah, and the Gospel
prophets/gospel/isa|lines.0: Standing and description: the Word of Allah and a spirit from Him, born of a chaste virgin without a father as a sign for the worlds; one of the messengers of firm resolve.
prophets/gospel/isa|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: speaking in the cradle as an infant; the miracles of healing the blind and the leper, raising the dead by Allah's permission and creating birds from clay; the plot to crucify him, and his rescue and being raised up to heaven ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ بَل رَّفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
prophets/gospel/isa|lines.2: The revealed scripture: the Gospel, confirming the Torah that came before it, and bringing glad tidings of the Seal of the Messengers ﴿وَمُبَشِّرًا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ﴾.
seal|title: Muhammad ﷺ — the Seal of the Prophets, and the Holy Qur'an
seal|subtitle: From his birth to the completion of the religion
seal|lines.0: Standing and description: the Seal of the prophets and messengers, a mercy to the worlds, the leader of the God-fearing, the one granted the Great Intercession and the Pond (al-Hawd) to which the believers will come.
seal|lines.1: The story in the Qur'an: the beginning of revelation in the cave of Hira (“Read”), proclaiming the call openly, the Isra' and Mi'raj (Night Journey and Ascension), the Hijra and the building of the Ummah, striving in the way of Allah, and the completion of the favour ﴿الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾.
seal|lines.2: The revealed scripture: the Holy Qur'an; the last of the revealed scriptures, the everlasting miracle, the guardian over the scriptures before it, and preserved by Allah's complete protection until the Day of Judgement ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ﴾.
seal/mawlid|title: The Year of the Elephant — the Prophet's birth
seal/mawlid|lines.1: Lineage: Muhammad son of 'Abd Allah son of 'Abd al-Muttalib son of Hashim, of Quraysh
seal/mawlid|lines.2: Event: the birth of the Prophet ﷺ in the Year of the Elephant
seal/bitha|title: The Prophetic mission — the beginning of revelation (age 40)
seal/bitha|lines.0: Place: Makkah al-Mukarramah (the cave of Hira)
seal/bitha|lines.1: Event: the descent of revelation and the beginning of the Message
seal/bitha|lines.2: First revealed: the opening of Surat al-'Alaq (“Read in the name of your Lord who created”)
seal/makki|lines.2: Core content: establishing belief ('aqidah) and tawhid
seal/makki|lines.4: Key events: proclaiming the call openly, the migration to Abyssinia, the boycott in the valley (Shi'b) of Abu Talib, the Year of Sorrow, the Isra' and Mi'raj and the obligation of the five daily prayers, and the two Pledges of al-'Aqabah
seal/makki/al-fatiha|subtitle: The Mother of the Qur'an and the Seven Oft-Repeated Verses
seal/makki/al-fatiha|lines.2: Its standing: the Mother of the Qur'an and the Seven Oft-Repeated Verses
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|title: The ayahs and what lies beneath them
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.0.0|text: Praising Allah for the perfection of His Essence and His Attributes
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.0.2|text: The Lord (al-Rabb): the One who nurtures others and brings them into being stage by stage
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.0.2.0|text: All creatures: it includes guiding them to what serves their interests, on which their survival in this world depends
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.0.2.1|text: Particular to the believers: through it He nurtures them, and removes from them the distractions and obstacles that stand between them and Him
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.1.0|text: All creatures, worldly only; it indicates neither Allah's love and pleasure nor His displeasure
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.1.1|text: Particular to the believers, a sign of Allah's love and pleasure; through it He gives respite to the disobedient and accepts the repentance of those who repent
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.1.2|label: The Throne is paired with mercy
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.1.2|text: ﴿الرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَىٰ﴾ + ﴿وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.2.2|text: A person may own a house and rent it out: they own it but do not rule in it; and a father rules over his children but does not own them
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.2.3|text: Because sovereignty is complete in the Hereafter, where everyone with a right receives their right
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.0|text: Divinity (servitude): from the servant to Allah — the cure for showing off (riya')
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.1|text: Lordship (seeking help): from Allah to the servant — the cure for arrogance
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.1.0|text: Asking for help, support and success in order to be able to do something and to be capable of doing it
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.1.1.0|text: Like a doctor all of whose operations have succeeded: they can be trusted, but there is no need to depend on them, since another doctor of the same skill exists
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.1.1.1|text: Like a doctor half of whose operations have succeeded, but who is the only one who performs them: one depends on them without trusting them fully
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.1.1.2|label: In Allah we trust and on Him we rely
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.1.1.2|text: Because He alone fulfils our needs, with a 100% success rate
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.1.2|text: A proof of the tawhid of divinity; tawhid of lordship without tawhid of divinity is like using one company's resources to serve another company — and to Allah belongs the highest example
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.2|label: Iyyaka ("You alone"): a particle of exclusivity
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.3.2|text: It is placed before the two verbs of worship and seeking help out of courtesy towards Allah, to magnify Him, out of concern and great care for Him, and to confine worship and seeking help to Allah: we worship none but Him and seek help from none but Him
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.4|text: Ayah 5 — asking for guidance through the attribute of mercy
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.4.0|text: The cure for misguidance and ignorance; it is paired with seeking help
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.4.0.0|text: All creatures: it includes guiding them to what serves their interests, on which their survival in this world depends
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.4.1|label: A road is a "sirat" (path) if it is
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.4.1.3|label: Wide enough for all who travel it
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.4.2|label: Does a human being have free choice, or are they driven?
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.4.2.0|text: In what happens within them, like heartbeats, and in what happens to them, like birth
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.4.2.1|text: In what they do, like eating and praying, with divine intervention either by granting success or by withdrawing support
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.5|text: Ayah 6 — the people of knowledge and action
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.5.0|label: Linking those who are favoured to the path
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.5.0.0|label: To remove the loneliness of being alone
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.5.0.0|text: For the soul feels lonely when alone
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.5.0.1|label: To urge one to set out and strive hard
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.5.0.1|text: To catch up with those who are favoured
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.5.0.2|label: To be counted among those who are favoured
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.5.0.3|label: To obtain the share of those who are favoured
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.6.2|label: Attributing favour to Allah, but not anger
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.6.2.0|text: whereas anger is not exclusive to Him
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.6.2.1|label: To honour those who are favoured
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d0|b0.6.2.2|label: To belittle and humiliate those who have earned anger
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d1|b0|text: Allah taught His servants how to ask Him
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d1|b0.0|text: Approaching Him through His names and attributes
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d1|b0.0.0|text: Affirming that praise belongs to Allah
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d1|b0.0.1|text: Mentioning the attributes of divinity, lordship, mercy and sovereignty
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d1|b0.0.2|text: Truly knowing that poison kills is shown only by avoiding it
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d1|b0.1|text: Approaching Him through one's servitude to Him
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.0.0|label: You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.0.0|text: Their goal is to worship Allah, and they seek Allah's help to grant them success in doing so
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.0.1|label: You alone we worship, but not: You alone we ask for help
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.0.1|text: They think they are left to themselves in their worship without any divine intervention — neither success granted to those who choose faith nor support withdrawn from those who choose disbelief; they do without the very core of worship, which is seeking help
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.0.2|label: Not: You alone we worship, but: You alone we ask for help
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.0.2|text: They seek Allah's help only to obtain their worldly shares, desires and aims
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.0.3|label: Neither: You alone we worship, nor: You alone we ask for help
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.0.3|text: Those who turn away from worshipping Him and seeking His help
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.1.0|text: Their deeds, outwardly and inwardly, are for the sake of Allah alone, and in accordance with the Shari'ah
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.1.1|text: Like ignorant devotees, such as one who thinks that a seclusion in which they abandon the Friday prayer and the congregation brings them closer to Allah
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.1.2|text: Like the obedience of show-offs, who do deeds that look righteous on the outside but do them to adorn themselves before people
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d2|b0.1.3|text: Their deeds are neither purely for the One worshipped nor in accordance with the Shari'ah
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d3|title: The axis of the Names and Attributes
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d3|b0|label: The axis of the Names and Attributes
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d3|b0|text: These four: Allah, the Lord (al-Rabb), the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful (al-Rahman al-Rahim), and the King (al-Malik)
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d3|b0.0|text: The Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, the Provider, the Giver, the Withholder, the One who harms, the One who benefits, the Constrictor, the Expander
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d3|b0.1|label: The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d3|b0.1|text: The Subtle, the All-Forgiving, the Appreciative, the Generous, the Forbearing, the Loving, the Praiseworthy, the Benevolent, the Accepter of Repentance, the Pardoner, the Compassionate
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d3|b0.2|text: The Judge, the Just, the All-Aware, the Magnificent, the Most High, the Great, the Preserver, the Sustainer, the Reckoner, the Watchful, the Responsive, the All-Encompassing, the Glorious, the Witness, the Truth, the Trustee, the Strong, the Protecting Friend, the Self-Sustaining, the Able, the All-Powerful, the Supremely Exalted, the Owner of Sovereignty, the Equitable, the Gatherer, the Self-Sufficient
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d4|b0|text: Emptying through glorification (tasbih) to cleanse the heart, then adorning through praise (hamd) to nourish it
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d4|b0.0|text: Declaring Allah, Glorified and Exalted, free of every imperfection: negating imperfections (emptying)
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d4|b0.1|text: Praising Allah for the perfection of His Essence and His Attributes (adorning)
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d4|b0.1.0|text: In times of ease and of hardship
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d4|b0.1.1|text: With the heart and the tongue; the challenge is for it to spring from the heart
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d4|b0.2|text: A kindness given in return for a blessing
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d4|b0.2.1|text: With the heart, the tongue and the limbs; the challenge is action
seal/makki/al-fatiha|d5|b0.1|text: Through stories and passing on reports, to confirm the knowledge
seal/makki/al-anam|subtitle: The great argument for tawhid and the confrontation with shirk
seal/makki/al-anam|lines.0: Type of Surah: Meccan, one of the seven long Surahs
seal/makki/al-anam|lines.2: Main axis: establishing the belief in pure tawhid, affirming Allah's lordship and divinity over His creation, refuting shirk, and arguing with the idolaters through rational and cosmic proofs.
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0|text: The great argument for tawhid and the confrontation with shirk
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.0|label: Signs of creation and of the dominion
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.0.0|text: For creating the heavens and the earth and making darkness and light
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.0.1|text: ﴿وَعِندَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ﴾
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.0.2|text: In plants, the stars, the breaking of dawn, and the stillness of the night
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.1|label: Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) argument with his people
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.1.0|label: Contemplating the dominion of the heavens and the earth
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.1.0|text: The star, the moon, the sun, and disowning the things that set
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.1.1|text: ﴿إِنِّي وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ حَنِيفًا﴾
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.1.2|text: Eighteen prophets in a single passage ﴿أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ فَبِهُدَاهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ﴾
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.2.0|label: What they forbade of crops and livestock
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.2.0|text: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ الْحَرْثِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ نَصِيبًا﴾
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.2.1|label: Making things lawful and unlawful is Allah's right alone
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.3.2|label: The prohibition of killing one's children for fear of poverty
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.3.4|label: The prohibition of taking a life except by right
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.3.6|label: Giving full measure and weight with justice
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.3.9|text: ﴿وَأَنَّ هَٰذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ﴾
seal/makki/al-anam|d0|b0.4|text: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾
seal/makki/yunus|lines.2: Main axis: affirming revelation and prophethood, answering those who deny the resurrection and the recompense, and Allah's ways (sunan) with the nations.
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.0|text: ﴿أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَبًا أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنْهُمْ﴾
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.0.0|text: In creating the heavens and the earth and governing all affairs
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.1|label: The cosmic signs and the answer to doubts
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.1.0|label: Night and day, the sun and the moon
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.1.1|label: Tawhid as innate nature in times of hardship
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.1.1|text: and the idolaters' ingratitude after being saved
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.2|label: Stories of the prophets and the patterns of salvation and destruction
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.2.0|label: Nuh (peace be upon him) and his people
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.2.1|label: Musa and Harun (peace be upon them) with Pharaoh
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.2.1|text: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ آيَةً﴾
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.2.2|label: The people of Yunus (peace be upon him)
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.2.2|text: ﴿إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ﴾
seal/makki/yunus|d0|b0.3|text: ﴿وَاتَّبِعْ مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيْكَ وَاصْبِرْ حَتَّىٰ يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ﴾
seal/hijra|lines.0: Event: the move from Makkah to Madinah al-Munawwarah
seal/hijra|lines.1: The turning point: the start of the Madinan era and of the Hijri calendar (1 AH)
seal/hijra|lines.2: The shift: from the stage of calling and patience to the stage of empowerment and building the state
seal/hijra|lines.3: His companion in the Hijra: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) ﴿إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا﴾
seal/hijra|lines.4: The first building: the Mosque of Quba' and then the Prophet's Mosque, and the brotherhood established between the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers)
seal/madani|lines.0: Duration: 10 years (from age 53 to age 63 / 11 AH = 632 CE)
seal/madani|lines.2: Core content: building the state, legislation and the rulings of fiqh
seal/madani|lines.4: General character: setting out transactions and rulings in detail, and building the Muslim society
seal/madani|lines.5: Key events: the Battle of Badr (2 AH), the Battle of Uhud (3 AH), the Battle of the Confederates (5 AH), the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah (6 AH), the Conquest of Makkah (8 AH), and the Farewell Pilgrimage (10 AH)
seal/madani/ghazawat|summary: Expeditions mentioned in the Holy Qur'an or about which its ayahs were revealed; from them the believer learns that victory comes from Allah, and that obedience and steadfastness are the way to it.
seal/madani/ghazawat/badr|lines.1: In the Qur'an: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ وَأَنتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ﴾ (Al Imran 123), and Surat al-Anfal was revealed about it.
seal/madani/ghazawat/badr|lines.2: The Day of the Criterion: the first major encounter between the Muslims and the idolaters, in which Allah gave victory to the believing few ﴿يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ﴾ (al-Anfal 41).
seal/madani/ghazawat/uhud|lines.1: In the Qur'an: ayahs of Surat Al Imran ﴿وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَقَاعِدَ لِلْقِتَالِ﴾ (Al Imran 121).
seal/madani/ghazawat/uhud|lines.2: The lesson: obeying the Messenger ﷺ is a cause of victory, and trial distinguishes the truthful ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ (Al Imran 140).
seal/madani/ghazawat/bani-nadir|lines.0: Time: the fourth year after the Hijra
seal/madani/ghazawat/bani-nadir|lines.1: In the Qur'an: Surat al-Hashr ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مِن دِيَارِهِمْ لِأَوَّلِ الْحَشْرِ﴾ (al-Hashr 2).
seal/madani/ghazawat/bani-nadir|lines.2: The cause: their breaking of the covenant with the Prophet ﷺ.
seal/madani/ghazawat/ahzab|title: The Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab, the Trench)
seal/madani/ghazawat/ahzab|lines.1: In the Qur'an: Surat al-Ahzab ﴿إِذْ جَاءُوكُم مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ وَمِن أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ (al-Ahzab 10).
seal/madani/ghazawat/ahzab|lines.2: The steadfastness of the believers: they dug the trench around Madinah, and said ﴿هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ (al-Ahzab 22).
seal/madani/ghazawat/fath|lines.1: In the Qur'an: ﴿إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ﴾ (al-Nasr 1).
seal/madani/ghazawat/fath|lines.2: Event: the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah as a conqueror, purified the Ka'bah of idols, and pardoned its people.
seal/madani/ghazawat/hunayn|lines.1: In the Qur'an: ﴿وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إِذْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ فَلَمْ تُغْنِ عَنكُمْ شَيْئًا﴾ (al-Tawbah 25).
seal/madani/ghazawat/hunayn|lines.2: The lesson: victory comes from Allah, not from great numbers.
seal/madani/ghazawat/tabuk|lines.0: Time: Rajab 9 AH; it was the Prophet's ﷺ last expedition
seal/madani/ghazawat/tabuk|lines.1: In the Qur'an: Surat al-Tawbah ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ فِي سَاعَةِ الْعُسْرَةِ﴾ (al-Tawbah 117), which is why it is called “the Expedition of Hardship”.
seal/madani/ghazawat/tabuk|lines.2: The lesson: mobilising in times of hardship, and distinguishing the truthful from the hypocrites.
seal/madani/al-baqara|subtitle: Establishing belief and building the state
seal/madani/al-baqara|lines.1: Taqwa in al-Baqarah = belief in the unseen
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0|label: Taqwa in al-Baqarah = belief in the unseen
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0.0.0|text: 3 ayahs: their qualities, the most important of which is belief in the unseen ﴿الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0.0.2|text: 13 ayahs: their evil is greater; they waver between the two groups
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0.0.3|label: The story of Adam (peace be upon him)
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0.0.3.0|label: Envy, arrogance, and disbelief despite knowledge
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0.0.3.1|label: The wisdom in creating Adam (peace be upon him), and the superiority of knowledge
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0.0.4.0|text: The traits that brought anger upon them
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0.0.4.1|text: Mixing truth with falsehood while knowing it ﴿وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾
seal/madani/al-baqara|d0|b0.0.5|text: The ideal model of one who fulfilled vicegerency on earth and submitted to Allah ﴿قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾

seal/madani/al-imran|d0|b0.0.0.1|label: The cosmic will: the will of the King

seal/madani/al-imran|d0|b0.0.2|label: The prohibition of taking disbelievers as allies instead of the believers
seal/madani/al-imran|d0|b0.0.2|text: ﴿لَّا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِن دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾
seal/madani/al-imran|d0|b0.1.0|text: ﴿رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا﴾
seal/madani/al-imran|d0|b0.1.1|text: ﴿وَمَن يَعْتَصِم بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾
seal/madani/al-imran|d0|b0.2.0|text: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ﴾
seal/madani/al-imran|d0|b0.2.2|text: ﴿إِن تُطِيعُوا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ﴾

seal/madani/an-nisa|subtitle: The Surah of justice, excellence and the rights of the vulnerable
seal/madani/an-nisa|lines.0: Type of Surah: Medinan (one of the seven long Surahs); it opens with a Meccan-style call: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾, to establish the common origin of humankind and to demand justice.
seal/madani/an-nisa|lines.1: Reason for the name: defending the rights of the vulnerable in general, and of women, orphans and slave women in particular, honouring women and setting out their rights in detail.
seal/madani/an-nisa|lines.2: How its beginning relates to its end: it begins with ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ﴾ and ends with ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جَاءَكُم بُرْهَانٌ﴾; it begins with inheritance and ends with the ayah of “al-Kalalah” (one who leaves neither parent nor child) to guarantee the right of the sister (the female).
seal/madani/an-nisa|lines.3: The prevailing name in the Surah: the King (al-Malik) (and with it: the Watchful, the Reckoner, the Witness, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the Sustainer, the Trustee, the All-Powerful); for the strong will refrain from wronging the weak only by feeling the watch of the Supreme King.

seal/madani/al-anfal|d0|b0.2.0|text: ﴿إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُم بِأَلْفٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ﴾
seal/madani/al-anfal|d0|b0.3|text: ﴿إِذَا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً فَاثْبُتُوا وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا﴾
seal/madani/al-anfal|d0|b0.5|text: ﴿وَإِن جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَهَا وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾
seal/madani/al-anfal|d0|b0.6.0|text: ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُم مِّن شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾

ummah/rashidun/caliph-5|lines.0: Length of the caliphate: he took it on after the martyrdom of his father 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and it lasted about six to seven months.
ummah/rashidun/caliph-5|lines.1: The Year of Unity ('Am al-Jama'ah): he stepped down to spare the blood of the Muslims and to unite the Ummah (41 AH).
ummah/umayyad|subtitle: The beginning of official, methodical recording
ummah/umayyad|summary: The Umayyad era saw a qualitative shift from limited individual recording to official, methodical recording under the patronage of the Islamic state, in response to geographical expansion and to preserve the Shari'ah.
ummah/umayyad/am-al-jamaa|lines.0: Length of the caliphate of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them): he took it on after the martyrdom of his father 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), and it lasted about six to seven months.
ummah/umayyad/am-al-jamaa|lines.1: Cause and motive: al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) stepped down to spare the blood of the Muslims, out of concern to unite the Ummah and end the years of division and fighting.
ummah/umayyad/am-al-jamaa|lines.2: The Prophetic glad tidings: the Prophet ﷺ said: “This son of mine is a leader (sayyid), and perhaps Allah will bring about reconciliation through him between two great groups of Muslims” (narrated by al-Bukhari).
ummah/umayyad/am-al-jamaa|lines.3: Reason for the name: in it the Muslims came together under a single leadership and pledged allegiance to Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with him), and so the Umayyad state began.
ummah/umayyad/umayyad-1|title: Why the shift towards official recording
ummah/umayyad/umayyad-1|lines.0: The death of the great memorisers: the state's territory expanded, and many of the Companions and senior Successors died or were martyred in the campaigns and in distant lands, so the scholars feared that knowledge would be lost with the death of those who carried it.
ummah/umayyad/umayyad-1|lines.1: The rise of strife and fabrication: disputes and sects emerged, and the first attempts at “fabricating hadith” (forged hadiths) began, which made it necessary to document the Sunnah, examine it critically and sift it.
ummah/umayyad/umayyad-2|lines.0: The decree of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz (d. 101 AH): the first to order official recording; he wrote to Abu Bakr ibn Hazm and the governors: “Look for whatever there is of the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and write it down, for I fear the fading away of knowledge and the passing of the scholars.”
ummah/umayyad/umayyad-2|lines.1: Imam Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri (d. 124 AH): the first to record hadith officially in response to the decree; he gathered the sunan and the reports in notebooks that the state copied and sent to the provinces.
ummah/umayyad/umayyad-2|lines.2: The nature of Umayyad recording: a general and comprehensive collection; the hadiths traced to the Prophet were written mixed with the legal opinions of the Companions and the sayings of the Successors, without precise arrangement into chapters or thematic separation between the branches of knowledge.
ummah/umayyad/umayyad-3|lines.0: Vowel dots (naqt al-i'rab): marking the endings of words with dots, at the hands of Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali (d. 69 AH).
ummah/umayyad/umayyad-3|lines.1: Letter-distinguishing dots (naqt al-i'jam): distinguishing similar letters with dots in the reign of 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, at the hands of Nasr ibn 'Asim and Yahya ibn Ya'mar.
ummah/abbasid|subtitle: The golden age of recording and classification
ummah/abbasid|summary: The Abbasid era represents the peak of maturity and intellectual flourishing, as the sciences moved from registers of general collection to independent, refined disciplines, arranged into chapters according to rigorous scholarly methods.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-1|title: The independence of the sciences and the method of classification
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-1|lines.0: Separation and specialisation of the sciences: the science of hadith became independent of fiqh, tafsir became a science in its own right, and the instrumental sciences arose to serve the sacred text.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-1|lines.1: From collection to classification: works were arranged according to thematic fiqh chapters (the Book of Purification, Prayer, Sales...) or according to the musnads of individual narrators.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-2|title: The recording of the four great schools of fiqh
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-2|lines.0: The Hanafi school: the recording of the fiqh of Abu Hanifah al-Nu'man (d. 150 AH) through the books of his students, especially the Zahir al-Riwayah of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-2|lines.1: The Maliki school: Malik ibn Anas (d. 179 AH) recorded his book al-Muwatta', combining hadith, fiqh and the practice of the people of Madinah.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-2|lines.2: The Shafi'i school: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i (d. 204 AH) recorded the book al-Umm in fiqh, and the book al-Risalah (the earliest work to reach us written on the principles of fiqh, usul al-fiqh).
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-2|lines.3: The Hanbali school: the recording of the fiqh of Ahmad ibn Hanbal (d. 241 AH) through his students, in addition to his great hadith encyclopaedia, the Musnad of Imam Ahmad.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-3|title: The revolution in hadith criticism and the six authentic books
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-3|lines.0: The two Sahihs: the compilation of Sahih al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH) and of Sahih Muslim (d. 261 AH) by his student; the most authentic books after the Qur'an, by the most precise standards of chains of narration (isnad) and verification.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-3|lines.1: The four Sunan: the Sunan of Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, completing the six recognised books.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-4|title: The instrumental sciences serving the text of the Qur'an and hadith
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-4|lines.0: Grammar and language: the flourishing of the schools of Basra and Kufa and the recording of the rules (such as al-Kitab by Sibawayh) to preserve the Arabic tongue and sound understanding.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-4|lines.1: Encyclopaedic tafsir: Imam Ibn Jarir al-Tabari (d. 310 AH) wrote his book Jami' al-Bayan 'an Ta'wil Ay al-Qur'an (The Comprehensive Exposition of the Interpretation of the Verses of the Qur'an) as the foremost reference of tafsir.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-4|lines.2: The science of the principles of fiqh (usul al-fiqh): the settling of the general rules for deriving rulings from their evidence.
ummah/abbasid/abbasid-4|lines.3: The science of narrators and of criticism and accreditation (al-jarh wa al-ta'dil): the rise of the critical tool for assessing the integrity and precision of narrators and protecting the Sunnah from intrusion.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams|title: The imams of Prophetic hadith, the Sahihs and the Sunan (3rd century AH)
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/bukhari|subti: The Commander of the Faithful in hadith
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/bukhari|lines: Name and place: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari, born in Bukhara; he travelled through the centres of the Islamic world gathering and scrutinising the Sunnah.
His greatest work: al-Jami' al-Musnad al-Sahih al-Mukhtasar min Umur Rasul Allah ﷺ wa Sunanihi wa Ayyamihi (Sahih al-Bukhari).
The most authentic book after the Book of Allah the Exalted, by the consensus of the scholars of the Ummah.

He required the highest degrees of authenticity: an unbroken chain, narrators of integrity and complete precision, proof of meeting and contemporaneity, and freedom from irregularity (shudhudh) and hidden defects ('illah).
He was known for the deep understanding in his precise chapter headings, so that it was said: “Al-Bukhari's fiqh is in his chapter headings.”
Other works: al-Adab al-Mufrad, al-Tarikh al-Kabir, and Khalq Af'al al-'Ibad.
Name and place: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Qushayri al-Naysaburi, a student of al-Bukhari and one of the leading hadith masters.
His greatest work: al-Musnad al-Sahih al-Mukhtasar bi-Naql al-'Adl 'an al-'Adl ila Rasul Allah ﷺ (Sahih Muslim).
The twin of Sahih al-Bukhari and the second most authentic book after the Holy Qur'an.
Distinguished by its fine arrangement and wording; it gathers the routes and wordings of a hadith in one place without splitting them, to make the narration and its fiqh easier to grasp.
He opened his book with a unique methodological introduction, counted among the oldest and most precise rules of the science of hadith terminology and the criticism of chains.
Other works: al-Kuna wa al-Asma' and al-Tamyiz.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/abu-dawud|sub: Imam of the Sunan and the fiqh of rulings
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/abu-dawud|lin: Name and upbringing: Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani, a student of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal; he travelled through the regions and settled in Basra.
His greatest work: Sunan Abi Dawud (containing about 5,274 hadiths).
A mainstay of jurists and mujtahids in deriving rulings; it is devoted to gathering the hadiths of legal rulings and of the lawful and the unlawful, rather than exhortations and stories.
He stated the grade of the hadiths: where there was serious weakness he pointed it out, and what he passed over in silence is fit to be used as evidence and for corroboration.
Al-Khattabi said of it: “The Book of Sunan by Abu Dawud is a noble book; no book like it has been written in the science of religion.”
Other works: Risalat Abi Dawud ila Ahl Makkah (Abu Dawud's letter to the people of Makkah), al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh, and al-Marasil.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/tirmidhi|subt: Compiler of the Sunan and the fiqh of hadith
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/tirmidhi|line: Name and upbringing: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn Sawrah al-Tirmidhi, the distinguished student of al-Bukhari, born and raised in Tirmidh in Transoxiana (the lands beyond the river).
His greatest work: al-Jami' al-Kabir (Sunan al-Tirmidhi).
He combined hadith with the fiqh of the Companions, the Successors and the jurists of the regions (Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad), showing who held by a hadith and who left it.
A pioneer in defining the grades and terms of hadith; the first to popularise the classification: (sahih, hasan, gharib, hasan sahih).
He took care to explain the hidden defects of hadiths and the names and kunyas of narrators with outstanding precision.
Other works: al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyyah (the greatest and best-known work on the description and character of the Prophet ﷺ), and al-'Ilal al-Kabir.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/nasai|subtitl: Critic of the Sunan, exacting in verification
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/nasai|lines.0: Name and upbringing: Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb ibn 'Ali al-Nasa'i, named after “Nasa” in Khurasan; he travelled in search of hadith to the Hijaz, Iraq, the Levant and Egypt, and settled in Egypt.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/nasai|lines.1: His greatest work: al-Sunan al-Sughra, called al-Mujtaba (Sunan al-Nasa'i), which he selected from his book al-Sunan al-Kubra.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/nasai|lines.3: Highly exacting about narrators; his condition was counted among the strictest of the authors of the Sunan, and after the two Sahihs his book has the fewest weak hadiths of the Sunan.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/nasai|lines.4: Close attention to the hidden defects of hadiths and to the differences in the narrators' wordings and routes.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/nasai|lines.5: Other works: al-Sunan al-Kubra, al-Du'afa' wa al-Matrukun, and 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah.
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/ibn-majah|sub: Completer of the six books, fine in arrangement
ummah/abbasid/hadith-imams/ibn-majah|lin: Name and upbringing: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Rab'i al-Qazwini, born in Qazvin; he travelled to Iraq, the Levant, the Hijaz and Egypt in search of hadith.
His greatest work: Sunan Ibn Majah (the sixth recognised book of the Sunan).
Distinguished by fine ordering, excellent arrangement into chapters and a smooth flow of fiqh (4,341 hadiths across 32 books and 1500 chapters).
Known for the “Zawa'id Ibn Majah” (Ibn Majah's additions): he alone narrated about 1339 hadiths not included by the authors of the five earlier books, among them sahih, hasan and da'if.
The majority of hadith imams (since the time of Ibn Tahir al-Maqdisi) settled on counting it as the sixth of the six books because of its benefits and unique additions.
Other works: Tafsir Ibn Majah (lost), and Tarikh Qazwin (History of Qazvin).
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams|title: The masters of tafsir and the encyclopaedias of Qur'anic exposition
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/tabari|subtit: The master of the exegetes and imam of the historians
Place and standing: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, a mujtahid imam who combined the sciences of tafsir, hadith, fiqh, the Qur'anic readings (qira'at) and history.
His greatest work in tafsir: Jami' al-Bayan 'an Ta'wil Ay al-Qur'an (Tafsir al-Tabari).
The foremost reference in tafsir based on transmitted reports (bi al-ma'thur), and the greatest of all the books of tafsir.
He cites the ayah, then presents the narrations with their chains from the Prophet ﷺ, the Companions and the Successors, discussing the chains and weighing between the opinions.
Precise use of the Arabic sciences, grammar and supporting lines of poetry, and explanation of the Qur'anic readings and of the fiqh of rulings.
His historical work: Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk (The History of the Messengers and Kings; Tarikh al-Tabari), the greatest reference on the history of the prophetic missions and of the Ummah.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/zamakhshari|s: Author of al-Kashshaf on Qur'anic eloquence
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/zamakhshari|l: Name and title: Mahmud ibn 'Umar al-Zamakhshari, given the title “Jar Allah” (Neighbour of Allah) because of his long residence in Makkah al-Mukarramah.
His greatest work: al-Kashshaf 'an Haqa'iq Ghawamid al-Tanzil wa 'Uyun al-Aqawil fi Wujuh al-Ta'wil.

One of the most prominent books of rhetorical and stylistic tafsir; it uncovered the secrets of the Qur'an's composition, the subtleties of its inimitability, and the sciences of meanings and of eloquence.
Use of the question-and-answer method (“If you say... I say...”) to turn over the facets of meaning and draw out its pearls.
Despite his Mu'tazili creed, which the scholars warned about, his book remained a reference no exegete can do without in understanding the secrets of eloquence and grammatical analysis.
Other works: Asas al-Balaghah, al-Mufassal fi 'Ilm al-'Arabiyyah, and al-Fa'iq fi Gharib al-Hadith.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/razi|subtitle: Author of the Great Tafsir, Mafatih al-Ghayb
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/razi|lines.0: Name and standing: Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn al-Husayn al-Razi, given the titles “Ibn Khatib al-Rayy” (son of the preacher of Rayy) and “the Imam”; he combined transmitted knowledge, reason and the principles of religion.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/razi|lines.1: His greatest work: Mafatih al-Ghayb (The Keys of the Unseen; al-Tafsir al-Kabir) in 32 volumes.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/razi|lines.3: Great attention to the science of “munasabat” (the connections between ayahs and Surahs), and to showing the thematic coherence of the Holy Qur'an.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/razi|lines.4: A vast rational encyclopaedia; he digressed into detailing the natural sciences and the rational proofs of tawhid.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/razi|lines.5: In it he responded to the philosophers and the Mu'tazilah, with careful investigation of questions of usul and fiqh.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/razi|lines.6: Other works: al-Mahsul fi 'Ilm Usul al-Fiqh, Asas al-Taqdis, and al-Matalib al-'Aliyah.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/qurtubi|subti: The master of juristic tafsir and the derivation of rulings
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/qurtubi|lines: Name and upbringing: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ansari al-Qurtubi, born in Cordoba in al-Andalus; he then travelled to Egypt, settled there and died in Minya.
His greatest work: al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an wa al-Mubayyin lima Tadammanahu min al-Sunnah wa Ay al-Furqan.
The greatest and most comprehensive encyclopaedia of juristic tafsir in Islamic history; it covered the ayahs of rulings and set out their questions in precise detail.
Scholarly fairness and devotion to the evidence; although a Maliki, he followed the stronger evidence and upheld it without partisanship for his school.
It contains a wealth of sciences: language, grammar, the readings, the abrogating and the abrogated, and the refutation of innovators.
Other works: al-Tadhkirah bi-Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah, and al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna.
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/ibn-kathir|su: The mainstay of tafsir by transmitted reports and of the criticism of narrations
ummah/abbasid/tafsir-imams/ibn-kathir|li: Name and standing: Isma'il ibn 'Umar ibn Kathir al-Qurashi al-Dimashqi, a student of Ibn Taymiyyah and al-Mizzi, and one of the great hadith masters and historians.
His greatest work: Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim (Tafsir Ibn Kathir).

The most complete model of the rule: “The soundest way of tafsir is to explain the Qur'an by the Qur'an, for what is stated briefly in one place is detailed in another; if that fails you, turn to the Sunnah, then to the sayings of the Companions, then of the Successors.”
Rigorous hadith criticism of the chains, distinguishing the authentic from the weak with the judgement of an expert hadith master.

A pioneering methodical campaign to refute the “Isra'iliyyat” (narrations from Jewish and Christian sources) and to warn against their oddities and legends in the stories of the prophets and past nations.
Other works: al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (The Beginning and the End; the greatest historical encyclopaedia of the Ummah), Jami' al-Masanid wa al-Sunan, and Tabaqat al-Shafi'iyyah.
ummah/mamluk|subtitle: The age of encyclopaedias and the great hadith commentaries
ummah/mamluk|summary: The Mamluk era represents the peak of encyclopaedic writing and of commentaries on the Prophetic Sunnah, as scholars devoted themselves to gathering the scattered sciences and preserving the Islamic heritage after the catastrophe of the fall of Baghdad:
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-1|title: The movement of the great hadith commentaries
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-1|lines.0: Complete attention to al-Bukhari's al-Jami' al-Sahih, to Sahih Muslim and to the Sunan, and careful establishment of the fine points of the chains, the language and the fiqh of rulings.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-1|lines.1: The appearance of Ibn Hajar's Fath al-Bari as the greatest hadith commentary, al-'Ayni's 'Umdat al-Qari, and al-Nawawi's commentary on Muslim.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-2|title: The flourishing of the sciences of hadith terminology and of narrators
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-2|lines.0: Refining the sciences of hadith and fixing the rules of terminology, building on the Muqaddimah of Ibn al-Salah (al-'Iraqi's Alfiyyah, and Ibn Hajar's Nukhbat al-Fikar).
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-2|lines.1: Expanding the biographies of narrators, the generations (tabaqat) and history (al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal, and al-Dhahabi's Siyar A'lam al-Nubala').
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-3|lines.0: The writing of comprehensive encyclopaedias of tafsir and the sciences of the Qur'an (al-Zarkashi's al-Burhan, and al-Suyuti's al-Itqan).
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-3|lines.1: Preserving the Arabic tongue and recording huge dictionaries such as Ibn Manzur's Lisan al-'Arab.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/nawawi|subtitl: Reviver of the Sunnah, master of the hadith scholars and the jurists
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/nawawi|lines.0: Name and upbringing: Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi, born in Nawa in Hawran in the Levant, he lived in Damascus; an imam of asceticism and of rigorous verification in fiqh and hadith.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/nawawi|lines.1: His greatest work in hadith commentary: al-Minhaj Sharh Sahih Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (al-Nawawi's commentary on Muslim).
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/nawawi|lines.3: A medium-length, comprehensive commentary in which he precisely set out the fiqh of the hadith, explaining the scholars' positions and the benefits of the chains, and the differences in the narrators' wordings and dialects.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/nawawi|lines.4: He supplied the chapter headings of Sahih Muslim, for which Muslim had not set explicit headings, and al-Nawawi's headings became the ones adopted by the commentators.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/nawawi|lines.5: He combined precision in hadith with careful comparative juristic analysis, in a clear and accessible style.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/nawawi|lines.6: Other encyclopaedic works: Riyad al-Salihin (the most widely spread hadith book in the Islamic world), al-Arba'un al-Nawawiyyah (the Forty Hadith), al-Majmu' Sharh al-Muhadhdhab (the greatest encyclopaedia of comparative fiqh), and Tahdhib al-Asma' wa al-Lughat.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/dhahabi|subtit: Imam of the hadith scholars and historian of Islam
Name and standing: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Uthman al-Dhahabi al-Dimashqi, the hadith scholar of his age, an expert in the hidden defects of hadith, the criticism of narrators and authentication.
The great works on biographies, narrators and history:

Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (Lives of the Noble Figures): the greatest and most delightful encyclopaedia of biographies of notable figures, scholars, caliphs and ascetics across the centuries, in 25 volumes.
Tarikh al-Islam wa Wafayat al-Mashahir wa al-A'lam: the comprehensive historical annals of the Muslim Ummah up to the year 700 AH.
Mizan al-I'tidal fi Naqd al-Rijal: the scale for criticising narrators, identifying the weak and the abandoned, and defending the trustworthy against accusations.
Works on the sciences of the Qur'an and hadith: Ma'rifat al-Qurra' al-Kibar 'ala al-Tabaqat wa al-A'sar, and al-Muqizah fi 'Ilm Mustalah al-Hadith.
Method: complete truthfulness, careful fairness in the biographies of opponents and allies alike, and elegant, incisive expression in criticising narrations and reports.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ibn-hajar|subt: The Commander of the Faithful in hadith and the last of the great hadith masters
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ibn-hajar|line: Name and standing: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Hajar al-Asqalani al-Kinani, chief judge of Egypt and Shaykh al-Islam of his time.
His greatest work: Fath al-Bari bi-Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari (its writing and dictation took 25 years, and it was said of it: “There is no hijra after the Fath”).

The summit of all commentaries on the Prophetic hadith; he resolved the difficulties of Sahih al-Bukhari, connected its suspended narrations (mu'allaqat), and covered all the routes and wordings of each hadith from the depths of the books of the Sunnah.
He derived thousands of benefits in fiqh, usul and language, and criticised the chains by the most precise standards of hadith science.
He opened it with a great introduction, Hady al-Sari, in which he set out the rules of al-Jami' al-Sahih and its chapter headings and defended its narrators against doubts.

Works on hadith and terminology: Nukhbat al-Fikar fi Mustalah Ahl al-Athar and its commentary Nuzhat al-Nazar (the most precise formulation of the rules of terminology), Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, Taqrib al-Tahdhib, and Bulugh al-Maram min Adillat al-Ahkam.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ayni|subtitle: Chief judge, and an encyclopaedic commentary on al-Bukhari
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ayni|lines.0: Name and upbringing: Mahmud ibn Ahmad al-'Ayni al-Hanafi, born in 'Ayntab near Aleppo; he travelled to Damascus and Cairo, and held the Hanafi judgeship and the office of market inspector (hisbah).
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ayni|lines.1: His greatest work: 'Umdat al-Qari fi Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari, in about 25 volumes.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ayni|lines.3: A huge encyclopaedia of language, grammatical analysis and fiqh; with it he rivalled his contemporary, the hadith master Ibn Hajar, writing at the same time as him.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ayni|lines.4: A unique method of arranging the commentary: he divides the commentary on each hadith into set sections: (its narrators, its vocabulary, its grammatical analysis, the drawing out of meanings and eloquence, then the derivation of legal rulings, the positions of the imams, and support for Hanafi fiqh with its evidence).
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ayni|lines.5: Extensive treatment of questions of grammar and morphology, the vocalisation of rare words, and the history of notable figures.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/ayni|lines.6: Other works: Sharh Sunan Abi Dawud, Maghani al-Akhyar fi Rijal Ma'ani al-Athar, and 'Iqd al-Juman fi Tarikh Ahl al-Zaman.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|subtitl: The last of the encyclopaedists and gatherer of the heritage
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|lines.0: Name and standing: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Suyuti, an encyclopaedic imam whose writings reached about 600 works in all fields.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|lines.1: The great works on tafsir and the sciences of the Qur'an:
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|lines.2: Al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an: the greatest encyclopaedic reference on the sciences of the Qur'an in history, in which he organised 80 kinds of the sciences of revelation.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|lines.3: Al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi al-Ma'thur: the widest collection of Prophetic hadiths and reports from the Companions on the tafsir of the ayahs of the Holy Qur'an.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|lines.4: Tafsir al-Jalalayn: with it he completed the tafsir of Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli; it is the best-known concise and accessible tafsir in circulation.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|lines.5: His efforts in commentaries on hadith and the Sunnah:
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|lines.6: Tadrib al-Rawi fi Sharh Taqrib al-Nawawi: a mainstay of the science of terminology; his commentaries on the Sunan of al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah; and his comprehensive book al-Jami' al-Saghir.
ummah/mamluk/mamluk-imams/suyuti|lines.7: Method: speed in gathering, precision in arrangement and classification, and preserving for the Ummah the texts of lost manuscripts.
ummah/ottoman|subtitle: Care for the Mushaf and the settling of the schools of law
ummah/ottoman|summary: The Ottoman era saw a major phase of legal and institutional stability, marked by care for the noble Mushaf, the codification of fiqh and the integration of commentaries:
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-1|title: The art of writing the noble Mushaf and Arabic calligraphy
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-1|lines.0: The writing of Mushafs reached the height of mastery and beauty in Istanbul at the hands of great Mushaf calligraphers (Hafiz Osman, Ahmed Karahisari).
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-1|lines.1: So much so that the historical saying spread: “The Qur'an was revealed in Makkah, recited in Egypt, and written in Istanbul.”
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-2|title: The settling of the Hanafi school and modern codification
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-2|lines.0: Hanafi fiqh was adopted as the official school for the judiciary and the state in all the provinces.
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-2|lines.1: The recording of the Majallat al-Ahkam al-'Adliyyah as the first modern codification of Islamic fiqh in the form of comprehensive legal articles.
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-3|title: The great commentaries and the glosses on tafsir and hadith
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-3|lines.0: The flourishing of carefully verified glosses on the books of earlier imams (Ibn 'Abidin's gloss in fiqh, and al-Jamal's gloss on al-Jalalayn in tafsir).
ummah/ottoman/ottoman-3|lines.1: The appearance of comprehensive encyclopaedias of tafsir such as al-Alusi's Ruh al-Ma'ani, and works compiling the readings and fixing the rules of tajwid.
timeline|2|label: The mission and the beginning of revelation
